chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from a number (of narrators), they raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When your brother comes to you, offer him food. If he does not eat, offer him water. If he does not drink, offer him ablution (wudu).
ai.seo_question: What is the proper sequence of offering food, water, and ablution to a visiting brother in Shia etiquette?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a hierarchical protocol for hospitality, prioritizing physical sustenance before spiritual purification. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in social interactions, where attending to a brother's immediate bodily needs is a prerequisite for engaging in ritual acts like *wudu*, thereby linking material care with spiritual readiness.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from a number, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When your brother comes over to you, so offer the food to him. So if he does not eat, so offer the water to him. So if he does not drink, so offer the ablution to him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from a number of our people who have narrated in a marfu‘ manner the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When your brother (in belief) comes to your house, offer him food, if he did not want, then offer him water and if he did not want water offer him wudu (to wash his face or perfume).’”
